subject: Preflight: HelixCare K8s node profiles, network stitch, and storage contract
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helixcare.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-11-01T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Preflight: HelixCare K8s node profiles, network stitch, and storage contract

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Before we lock Sprint 1 and get the Field Ops visit on calendar, we need to confirm a few on-prem details so the SOW and BOM don't move mid-provisioning. Quick asks below; can you confirm by end of week?

1) Node inventory: can you attach the CSV that lists chassis model, NICs, disk types (nvme vs sata), and CPU model per rack? We need per-node SKU to map to our node profiles.
2) Network: will HelixCare provide a routed VLAN (L3) with a /22 for the cluster, or will you expect us to NAT and do overlay? Any egress proxy or upstream filtering?
3) Storage tiering and retention: for training/embeddings cache we plan ephemeral NVMe. For model artifacts and checkpointing we need a durable block store that supports snapshots. Preferred backup cadence? snapshot retention?
4) KMS: do you have a customer-managed KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS / Vault HSM)? Will we be allowed to create service principals/roles?
5) Timeline constraints: any black-out windows for maintenance or rack access restrictions?

I attached a short template you can fill (helixcare-node-inventory.xlsx) and a blank network sketch to annotate.

Next steps: if the inventory + VLAN plan look standard we will:
- propose node profiles (gpu, cp-heavy, infra),
- propose PV class mapping (ephemeral local, encrypted blockstore, archive),
- ship SOW-draft-v3 for procurement review.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helixcare.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@helixcare.com>
Date: 2029-11-01T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: HelixCare K8s node profiles, network stitch, and storage contract

Monica —

Thanks for the checklist. Attached is the filled node inventory and a rough network diagram (network-stitch-diagram.pdf). High-level answers inline:

1) Node inventory: attached. Rack-level power is 2P redundant. Most nodes are Dell R750 with Nvidia A30s (12x NVMe per chassis), 2x 100G Mellanox per node.
2) Network: We'll hand over a routed L3 segment (we can allocate a /22) with BGP to your edge router during the field install. Egress filtering is handled on our upstream firewall — we will provide a contact for the security team. No forced HTTP proxy.
3) Storage: Checkpointing goes to a SAN-backed blockstore (NetApp) exposed via iSCSI over dedicated VLAN with snapshot capability. Snapshot cadence daily with 14-day retention; long-term archive via S3-compatible archive monthly.
4) KMS: We have a HashiCorp Vault cluster (internal HSM-backed) and will provide read-only tokens and a service account for Redwood to use. We prefer you leverage our Vault rather than provisioning a new cloud KMS.
5) Timeline: Rack access is 0900–1700 local, Mon–Fri; no weekend installs without 7-day notice.

I'll loop procurement (procurement@helixcare.com) and Priya for SOW cadence. Let us know if you need any more detail on NVMe endurance or egress ACLs.

—Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, HelixCare

Attachments: helixcare-node-inventory.xlsx, network-stitch-diagram.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helixcare.com>
Date: 2029-11-02T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: HelixCare K8s node profiles, network stitch, and storage contract

Folks — quick technical clarifications from infra side:

- NVMe: thanks for the inventory. For our GPU-worker profile we expect local NVMe for tokenizer/kv cache. Can HelixCare confirm whether NVMe is presented as raw devices (to be formatted) or pre-provisioned partitions? We need write endurance numbers to pick cache TTLs.

- iSCSI SAN: Is multipath configured on the host side? If so, what MPIO driver/version and do you have a preferred connector/user? We want to ensure our CSI driver supports the pathing.

- Vault access: we will need a service principal that can request unwrap tokens and fetch keys for blockstore encryption. Can Alex confirm scope? If Vault ACLs are read-only we may need an allowlist for calls per minute.

- Network: for the routed VLAN and BGP session — what ASN and neighbor IP do you plan to use? Also: public egress will be NATed by HelixCare; do you expose any public IPs for inbound callbacks (webhooks) that Redwood routing should be aware of?

I can draft node profile recommendations once we verify NVMe presentation and iSCSI multipath. Vanessa — can you scope the PV class mapping once KMS constraints are clear?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@helixcare.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helixcare.com>
Cc: procurement@helixcare.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-11-04T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: HelixCare K8s node profiles, network stitch, and storage contract

Hi Monica / Alex —

Procurement here. A couple items to keep the SOW moving:

- We need an estimated one-time hardware install window (hours on site) and a not-to-exceed travel day count for your field team for budget approval.
- Please confirm whether Redwood requires privileged access to Vault (we need to list required access in the security addendum).
- Pricing: we prefer to see SOW-draft-v3 with line items (field hours, per-node software seat, recurring storage rate). Can you provide an initial estimate?

If you can get the SOW draft to us by Tuesday we can try to fast-track PO issuance.

Thanks —
Priya
Senior Procurement Manager, HelixCare
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@helixcare.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@helixcare.com>, procurement@helixcare.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-11-05T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: HelixCare K8s node profiles, network stitch, and storage contract

Hi all —

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Alex and Priya. High-level plan and answers to procurement:

Install window / field hours: 2 engineers x 3 days onsite (estimated 48 staff-hours) for rack-mount, staging, and BGP edge configuration. Travel: 2 round-trip days per engineer (not-to-exceed 4 travel days). We will include a contingency half-day for troubleshooting.

Vault access: Redwood requests a service account with the ability to read unwrap tokens and fetch key metadata. We do not require write privileges to Vault. If HelixCare wants an allowlist on calls per minute we can throttle client-side; typical usage is <5 calls/minute during startup, <1/minute steady-state for secrets fetch. Please add this scope to the security addendum.

Pricing: we'll circulate SOW-draft-v3 with line items by end of day Tuesday. Early estimate (paper exercise only): one-time field services $18,000; per-node software seat $120/node/month; storage overlay (managed snapshots & archives) $0.015/GB/month. Final numbers in SOW.

Technical notes / next actions for infra:
- Alex: confirm NVMe presentation (raw devices vs pre-partitioned) and MPIO config.
- HelixCare security: provide Vault token for our staging account and contact for firewall ACLs.
- Redwood: Karthik & Vanessa will propose node profiles and PV class mapping in a follow-up doc (will share by 2029-11-08).

Attachments: SOW-draft-v3.docx (placeholder — we will attach the completed doc Tues).

Thanks — looking forward to the on-site.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOW-draft-v3.docx
